justifications.c1: Independent UK figures ≥£5k: Inova Stone (worktop maker) fined £60k + £7,363 costs (search-confirmed across kbbreview, HSE, Plant Services, Slough Express), Stoneworld £30k, Warmsworth £18k, plus HSE stop-work orders in 2026; civil awards (£3.5m, >£400k) are not engineered stone, and none of the fines is shown to turn on water suppression being off.
justifications.c2: HSE plans 1,000+ fabricator visits in 2026 (roughly one inspection per site per year) and Thorax cases 'reported dry-cutting', but the file records no data on how often water is off during cuts and no required monthly or weekly check.
justifications.c3: File states no workshop logs water-on time today and the control is observation and inspection; only free supplier training (Caesarstone, Cosentino) exists, so the sensor adds a new cost rather than replacing one.
justifications.c4: HSE May 2026 engineered-stone COSHH guidance rules out dry cutting, with a 1,000-visit campaign and stop-work notices (press release search-confirmed), plus Inova prosecution and a Victorian prosecution over wet cutting; but no rule requiring records of water-suppression use is cited.
justifications.c5: Buyers are small fabricator owners with limited budgets (Thorax: 'small companies'); no job advert or role description evidences a budget holder, and the universe is only ~650 UK fabricators.
justifications.c6: Slab suppliers (Caesarstone Master of Stone, Cosentino) push safety training to fabricators, but there is no evidence they or any dealer sell or bundle monitoring technology; machinery dealers and fit-testers were not searched.
justifications.c7: No comparable product, price or paying customer found (one query, 'none surfaced'); dust-monitor prices not found, so willingness to pay is entirely unevidenced.
justifications.c8: Off-the-shelf LoRaWAN flow sensors (~€54–79 per search, file cites €59) and EM300-DI (€64–120) exist, but the per-tool BOM with a CT node exceeds ~£100, and slurry recycling plus hand tools on flexible hoses create fouling and bypass risk.
justifications.c9: Inspections recur and silicosis claims have long latency, so a record has some ongoing value, but there is no record-keeping duty for water use and no comparable subscription pricing.
justifications.c10: Regulator releases (HSE ?p=8009, ?p=8215), trade press (Stone World, Stone Specialist, kbbreview), NHS/Thorax case series, APPG report, and claimant-firm claim pages and client stories (Leigh Day, Irwin Mitchell, Thompsons).

weakest: No evidence anyone pays for anything similar: no flow-proving or dry-cutting monitor product, price or customer was found, and no existing paid workaround is being replaced.
